note: Reviews student and teacher assistance, adaptive learning and commercial tools, with the datasets and benchmarks behind each, plus the deployment risks.
title: Large Language Models for Education: A survey and outlook

reading.body:
This survey reviews how language models are used to assist students and teachers, covering adaptive learning tools, the datasets and benchmarks used to evaluate them, and the deployment risks involved.

Education is one of the sectors where AI adoption is furthest from a compute or infrastructure story and closest to a pedagogy story, since the tools reviewed here are mostly about personalizing instruction and supporting teachers rather than automating a task outright. The inclusion of commercial tools alongside research systems suggests the gap between lab research and classroom deployment in this sector is relatively narrow compared to other fields.

The survey does not report original outcome data on whether these tools improve learning, only that it catalogs what has been built and what risks researchers have flagged.

explain_beginner: This paper examines how large language models, the technology behind tools like ChatGPT, can improve education. Researchers looked at how these AI systems help both students and teachers, personalize learning for individual needs, and reviewed existing educational products using this technology. They also identified potential problems with using these tools in schools and suggested areas for future improvement. The work matters because it helps educators understand how to responsibly adopt this powerful technology to create better learning experiences.
explain_business: This analysis demonstrates that LLM-based educational tools span multiple market segments from student assistance to teacher augmentation to adaptive learning platforms. Understanding the datasets and benchmarks used to evaluate these systems helps stakeholders assess technology maturity and competitive positioning. The documented deployment risks and challenges indicate where regulatory compliance and safety mechanisms become necessary business considerations. For educational institutions and edtech companies, this roadmap clarifies which applications are production-ready versus requiring further development before implementation.
explain_practitioner: This survey systematically reviews LLM applications across educational domains including student tutoring, teacher support, and personalized instruction systems. The authors catalog relevant datasets, benchmarks, and technological implementations across each application area. The study identifies and categorizes deployment challenges and safety concerns specific to educational contexts. Key findings include assessment of current commercial solutions and their underlying capabilities, gaps in existing evaluation frameworks, and research priorities for advancing educational AI systems responsibly.
